requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit is enabled and active, has the required ExecStart, and remained active after reboot. The current-boot journal confirms successful startup.

requirements.requirement: Run the service under a dedicated inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: inventorysvc is a dedicated system account with its own group, private home directory, and non-login shell. Both systemd configuration and the observed process identity show the worker running as inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 reports CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The supplied POSIX-shell worker retained its prepared checksum and runs successfully under native systemd without added packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart service was observed, reboot was acknowledged, node unavailability was captured, the boot ID changed from a70d7f83-6867-4c91-851d-7a1228689bb3 to ad5d480e-6da4-4163-94ee-4b9a397fd788, and the enabled service, account, executable checksum, OS, and kernel were recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The worker has no application-level output or data interface, so recovery evidence is necessarily limited to its process, unit, account, executable integrity, and current-boot journal. No separate cluster state exists in the single-node topology.

The final passwd -S probe produced no visible status text, although the non-login shell, system UID, dedicated group, and observed runtime identity directly establish the required dedicated service-account behavior.
Requirement platform-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-service-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: The final system is clean: no failed services, package health remains good, and no new listener or unexplained persistent residue appears. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred: cmd-6f6ab6dd93d94b39 invoked the worker with --help, but the worker has no help mode and continued running as an unmanaged process. That transient process was fully stopped by the corrective cleanup in cmd-15f669bdb7f1432f. All other observed mutations were directly tied to creating the account and service, enabling it, or performing the mandatory restart protocol.
